model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral, reusable governance-role overlay for typed dependency and downstream-impact assertions: who may issue, steward, review, approve, observe, analyse and except such assertions, under which purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers, with explicit accountability boundaries that leave authorization decisions, enforcement and audit storage to referenced models.
model.scope_statement: This bounded slice of WM-XCT-037 models the governance-role layer that attaches to a dependency or impact assertion: the generic role archetypes and their accountability boundaries; binding of those archetypes to agents with delegation, term and scope; mandatory purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers; review and approval decision records; contested-assertion handling; exception (waiver) grants; and declarative record-governance markers (sensitivity classification, retention-class reference, legal-hold marker) that refer outward for execution. It is a mixin: it carries no dependency-graph typing, traversal, blast-radius computation or criticality scoring of its own, and it neither renders nor enforces authorization decisions and is not an audit store.
in_scope: Generic governance role archetypes for dependency and impact assertions (issuer, endpoint steward, reviewer, approver, observer, analyst, exception authority) with explicit accountability boundaries
Role-to-agent binding, delegation chains, scope of authority, and validity terms expressed as qualified attributions
Segregation-of-duties declarations: incompatible duty pairs, two-person conditions and self-review prohibitions, expressed as declarative constraints for an external decision point to evaluate
Mandatory purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers on every governance act, expressed as references to external code lists rather than embedded polity doctrine
Review, approval, rejection and re-review decision records attached to a dependency or impact assertion
Contested-assertion handling: counter-assertion, no-assertion, dispute state and the authority competent to resolve
Time-bounded exception and waiver grants with the accountable authority, conditions and expiry
Declarative record-governance markers on governance records: sensitivity/access classification, retention-class reference and legal-hold marker
out_of_scope: Dependency edge typing, dependency-graph construction, transitive closure, blast-radius or impact-propagation computation - owned by the WM-XCT-037 core assertion structure this overlay mixes into
Authorization decision rendering and enforcement (policy decision point, policy enforcement point, obligations and advice) - owned by the referenced access-control and policy model
Audit trail storage, log integrity, non-repudiation evidence and audit retrieval - owned by the referenced audit and evidence model
Minting or lifecycle management of party, organization and agent identities - owned by the referenced party/agent identity model

Execution of destruction, disposition, transfer or hold release, and the legal determination that a hold applies - owned by the referenced records retention and disposition model and the adopting Dimension's legal function
Lawful basis determination, data-subject rights handling and privacy impact assessment - owned by the referenced privacy/personal-data processing model
Jurisdiction definitions, polity doctrine, constitutional or treaty interpretation - referenced as codes from an external jurisdiction registry
Criticality analysis methodology, supplier risk scoring and supply-chain risk treatment selection
Runtime notification delivery, subscription transport and messaging semantics for observers

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-XCT-037 core dependency and impact assertion structure (typed edges, traversal, propagation)
boundary_notes.distinction: This overlay answers who is accountable for an assertion and under what governance act it became usable; it does not define what the assertion means as a graph edge, nor how impact propagates. Edge semantics follow patterns such as the SPDX Relationship class (from, to, relationshipType, completeness, startTime/endTime) and CycloneDX dependency structures, which remain owned by the core.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Access-control and authorization policy model (policy administration, decision and enforcement points)
boundary_notes.distinction: Role archetypes and segregation-of-duties statements recorded here are declarative inputs - comparable to attributes supplied by a policy information point. Rendering an authorization decision (policy decision point), enforcing it (policy enforcement point) and discharging obligations or advice are owned externally; nothing in this model grants access.

Decision, contestation and exception records here are governance artifacts that state an outcome and its accountable authority. They are not the audit trail: append-only logging, tamper-evidence, log retention and audit reporting are owned by the referenced audit model.

This model carries only a retention-class reference and a boolean-plus-provenance legal-hold marker on its own governance records. Approval of disposition authority, execution of destruction, extension of retention for litigation, and reporting of unauthorized disposition are owned by the records model and the adopting Dimension's records officer.

Role bindings reference agent identifiers (person, organization or software agent) resolved elsewhere; this model neither mints identifiers nor manages the identity lifecycle. It uses the qualified-attribution pattern to attach a role to an already-identified agent.

Purpose qualifiers here are governance-act purposes drawn from an external code list. Determination of lawful basis, purpose-limitation compatibility assessment, controller/processor allocation and records of processing activities are owned by the privacy model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk management, change and release management models
boundary_notes.distinction: An exception grant recorded here states that a named authority accepted a deviation for a bounded period. Risk assessment methodology, risk-acceptance criteria, remediation tracking and change-advisory workflow remain in the risk and change models; this model records the governance outcome, not the treatment plan.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative pattern for qualified attribution: prov:Agent, prov:wasAttributedTo, prov:qualifiedAttribution, prov:Role and prov:hadRole let a role be attached to an agent for a specific influence, and prov:actedOnBehalfOf models delegation. Grounds role binding, delegation and provenance of governance acts.

sources.title: Relationship - SPDX Specification 3.0.1 (Core Model)
sources.relevance: Defines a dependency assertion as a first-class Element with from/to/relationshipType, optional completeness, startTime and endTime, and explicit NoneElement versus NoAssertionElement semantics. Grounds the boundary between edge semantics (core) and governance overlay, and the modelling of 'no assertion' as a legitimate contested or unknown state.

sources.title: CreationInfo - SPDX Specification 3.0.1 (Core Model)
sources.relevance: Requires every Element to carry created (DateTime), createdBy (Agent: Person, Organization or SoftwareAgent) and specVersion, and distinguishes the modelled creation time from the time the data was generated. Grounds the issuer archetype and the event-time versus ingestion-time separation.

sources.title: Annotation - SPDX Specification 3.0.1 (Core Model)
sources.relevance: Models a typed, separately-attributed assertion about an existing Element with its own creationInfo and subject. Grounds reviewer and analyst commentary as first-class, independently attributed records rather than mutations of the underlying dependency assertion.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Separates issuer, holder, subject and verifier roles, adds validFrom/validUntil validity periods and credentialStatus, and distinguishes verification (authorship) from validation (fit for a verifier's purpose). Grounds the issuer archetype, time-bounded role bindings and the reviewer/approver split.

sources.title: ODRL Vocabulary & Expression 2.2
sources.relevance: Defines Party functions (assigner, assignee, and odrl:function roles such as informedParty, trackingParty, dataController) and constraint left operands including odrl:purpose, odrl:spatial, odrl:recipient and odrl:industry. Grounds purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers and the observer archetype without embedding polity doctrine.

sources.title: RFC 8126 / BCP 26 - Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs
sources.relevance: Establishes registration-governance archetypes: Designated Expert (reviewer) who must coordinate review, respond in bounded time, defend decisions and recuse on conflict of interest; Change Controller as the party authorized to approve future modification; graduated approval policies; entry states (reserved, deprecated, obsolete); and an appeals path for contested expert decisions.

sources.title: RFC 3339 - Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative date-time grammar requiring two-digit seconds and an explicit time-offset of Z or ±HH:MM, with -00:00 reserved for unknown local offset. Grounds the model's timestamp rule for governance decision, effective and observation times.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0 Plus Errata 01, Core Specification
sources.relevance: Separates policy administration (PAP), decision (PDP), enforcement (PEP) and attribute supply (PIP), with obligations and advice discharged by the enforcement point. Provides the normative basis for keeping authorization decisions and enforcement outside this model while it supplies declarative role and duty attributes.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 - Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.version_or_date: Rev. 5, September 2020, updates through 10 December 2020; DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-53r5
sources.relevance: Control catalogue organised into families including Access Control (AC), Audit and Accountability (AU), Risk Assessment (RA), Program Management (PM) and Supply Chain Risk Management (SR). Establishes that access control, audit and accountability, and supply-chain governance are distinct control families with distinct owners, supporting the separation of this model from access and audit models.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2 - Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.relevance: Defines an explicit role set - authorizing official, system owner, common control provider, information owner/steward, risk executive function, security and privacy officers - and an authorization decision that constitutes accepted risk, tracked with a plan of action and milestones. Grounds the approver, endpoint steward and exception-authority archetypes.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 - Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.version_or_date: Rev. 1, May 2022, updates through 1 November 2024; DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-161r1-upd1
sources.relevance: Requires organizations to define supply-chain-relevant roles across enterprise, mission and system levels, including roles applicable within suppliers, developers, system integrators and external service providers, and places ownership and accountability for dependency risk with organizational leadership. Grounds cross-boundary endpoint stewardship.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center Glossary - separation of duty
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.version_or_date: Glossary entry sourced from NIST SP 800-192, NISTIR 8403 and NIST IR 8539; accessed 5 September 2026
sources.relevance: Defines separation of duty as preventing any single user holding privileges sufficient for unilateral misuse, and distinguishes static separation (conflicting roles never assigned to the same user), dynamic separation (enforced at access time, e.g. two-person rules) and history-based variants. Grounds the incompatible-duty declarations.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 27 April 2016, consolidated text on EUR-Lex
sources.relevance: Article 4(7)/(8) controller and processor; Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation; Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation; Article 5(2) accountability; Article 6 lawful basis; Article 30 records of processing activities. Grounds mandatory purpose qualifiers, retention referral and the requirement that personal data in role bindings be minimised and justified.

sources.title: Unauthorized Dispositions of Federal Records
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.version_or_date: Current guidance page, accessed 5 September 2026; cites 44 U.S.C. 3106 and 36 CFR Part 1230
sources.relevance: Establishes that unlawful removal, deletion, alteration or destruction of records must be reported to the Archivist under 44 U.S.C. 3106 and 36 CFR Part 1230, and that a records-management oversight function - not the originating system - owns adjudication. Grounds the legal-hold marker and the outward referral of disposition execution.

sources.title: ECMA-424 - CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification
sources.relevance: Standardises structured inventory of components, services and dependencies together with metadata, annotations, external references, lifecycle context and claims/attestations for conformance. Confirms that dependency structure and attestation metadata are separable concerns and that dependency records routinely carry authoring and supplier attribution.

bundles.name: Accountability and Role Assignment
bundles.description: The generic governance role archetypes that may attach to a typed dependency or downstream-impact assertion, their accountability boundaries, the constraints that keep incompatible duties apart, and the way an archetype is bound to a specific agent for a bounded scope, term, purpose and jurisdiction.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative practice consistently separates the party that asserts a fact, the party accountable for the endpoint the fact concerns, the party that reviews it and the party that accepts residual risk. SPDX requires every assertion element to carry createdBy attribution; PROV-O supplies the qualified-attribution and delegation pattern; the Verifiable Credentials model separates issuer from verifier; RFC 8126 separates the designated expert from the change controller; NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2 names authorizing official, owner and steward as distinct roles; and NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 requires those roles to be defined across organizational boundaries including suppliers and integrators. Without this bundle a dependency assertion is unattributable and its governance is unfalsifiable.

layers.name: Role Archetypes and Accountability Boundaries
layers.description: Definition of the reusable, polity-neutral role archetypes for dependency and impact governance, the endpoint-stewardship split that arises because a dependency has two ends under potentially different owners, and the declarative separation-of-duties constraints that limit which archetypes one agent may hold at once.

findings.name: Governance role archetype catalogue
findings.description: A governed, extensible catalogue of the seven generic archetypes an agent may occupy with respect to a dependency or impact assertion - issuer, endpoint steward, reviewer, approver, observer, analyst and exception authority - each with a definition, the governance acts it may originate, and the acts it is explicitly not accountable for. Archetypes are abstract role concepts in the PROV-O sense; the adopting Dimension maps them to its own job titles, committees and delegated bodies without this model prescribing an organizational form.

questions.text: What exactly does each governance role archetype mean for a dependency or impact assertion, and which governance acts is it competent to originate?
answer_data: Archetype code and canonical label
Normative definition text
Enumerated competent governance acts (assert, annotate, review, approve, reject, except, observe)
Enumerated explicitly-excluded acts
Citation to the grounding source for the archetype

questions.text: Where does one archetype's accountability stop and the next archetype's begin, so that no act is unowned and no act is doubly owned?
answer_data: Accountability boundary statement per archetype
Handover point between adjacent archetypes
Escalation target when an act falls outside every declared archetype
Flag for acts deliberately left to a referenced model

questions.text: How may an adopting Dimension add a locally required archetype without breaking interoperability of the generic set?
answer_data: Extension namespace for local archetype codes
Required parent archetype (specialisation link)
Registration policy applied to the local extension
Deprecation status of superseded local codes

questions.text: How does a given archetype map onto external role vocabularies so that governance data remains exchangeable?
answer_data: Mapping target vocabulary identifier (for example a PROV role IRI or an ODRL party function)
Mapping relation strength (exact, broader, narrower, related)
Known semantic mismatch note
Mapping provenance and reviewer

data_elements.name: Role archetype code
data_elements.description: Stable code identifying one generic governance role archetype in the catalogue.

data_elements.name: Competent governance acts
data_elements.description: Enumerated set of governance acts the archetype may originate for a dependency or impact assertion.

data_elements.name: Excluded acts and referral target
data_elements.description: Acts the archetype must not perform locally, each paired with the referenced model or external body that owns them.

data_elements.name: Parent archetype reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the generic archetype that a Dimension-local archetype specialises.

data_elements.name: External role vocabulary mapping
data_elements.description: Alignment from an archetype code to an external role or party-function identifier, with mapping strength.

artifacts.name: Dependency governance role archetype register
artifacts.description: The governed code list of role archetypes with definitions, competent and excluded acts, parent links, external mappings and registration status. Published as a versioned controlled vocabulary independent of any serialisation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each entry is identified by its stable archetype code within the register namespace, resolvable as a governed IRI; the register itself carries the adopting Dimension's master-system identifier for the vocabulary. Superseded codes are retained with a deprecated status rather than removed.

findings.name: Endpoint stewardship and cross-boundary accountability
findings.description: A dependency assertion has at least two ends, and the source and target may sit under different owners, organizations or contracts. This finding models the endpoint-steward binding for each end of the assertion, the case where the counterparty end is outside the adopting Dimension's control, and the resulting accountability asymmetry: an issuer may assert a dependency on an endpoint it does not steward, but cannot bind that endpoint's steward to any obligation.

questions.text: Which agent is the accountable steward of each end of this dependency, and is that end inside or outside the adopting Dimension's control boundary?
answer_data: Endpoint role (source or target)
Steward agent reference
Control-boundary classification (internal, contracted external, uncontracted external, unknown)
Contract or agreement reference where the end is external
Evidence that the steward accepted the stewardship

questions.text: Has the counterparty steward acknowledged the asserted dependency, and what is the governance status when it has not?
answer_data: Acknowledgement state (acknowledged, disputed, unacknowledged, not sought)
Acknowledgement timestamp and acknowledging agent
Unilateral-assertion flag
Note that unacknowledged assertions create no obligation on the counterparty

questions.text: When an endpoint is itself a composite, at which level is stewardship asserted and how does it decompose?
answer_data: Asserted stewardship granularity (system, component, dataset, service, other)
Parent endpoint reference
Inherited-versus-explicit stewardship flag
Decomposition depth limit declared by the adopting Dimension

questions.text: What happens when no steward can be identified for an endpoint that a critical impact path traverses?
answer_data: Unstewarded-endpoint marker
Interim accountable agent reference
Escalation target and due date
Link to any exception grant covering the gap

data_elements.name: Endpoint steward binding
data_elements.description: Association of one end of a dependency assertion with the agent accountable for that endpoint.

data_elements.name: Control-boundary classification
data_elements.description: Whether the endpoint lies inside the adopting Dimension, under contract, outside any agreement, or is unknown.

data_elements.name: Counterparty acknowledgement state
data_elements.description: Whether the steward of the far endpoint has acknowledged, disputed or not responded to the assertion.

data_elements.name: Unstewarded endpoint marker
data_elements.description: Flag with escalation reference indicating that no accountable steward has been identified for an endpoint.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Endpoint stewardship is expressed entirely as reference data: a pair of pointers from an existing dependency assertion to agent identifiers that are minted and maintained in the referenced party/agent identity model, qualified by a control-boundary code and an acknowledgement state. Materialising a separate stewardship artifact would duplicate the authoritative party register and the core assertion's own from/to endpoints, creating two divergent copies of the same relationship. The correct projection is inline qualification of the assertion, so this finding declares no artifact of its own.

findings.name: Segregation-of-duties declarations for dependency governance
findings.description: Declarative statements of which archetype combinations one agent must not hold simultaneously for the same assertion, which acts require two distinct persons, and where self-review or self-approval is prohibited. These are constraint declarations supplied as attributes to an external decision point; this model records the rule and any recorded conflict observation, and never blocks an operation itself.

questions.text: Which pairs or sets of role archetypes are declared incompatible for the same agent on the same dependency or impact assertion?
answer_data: Incompatible archetype set
Separation mode (static, dynamic, history-based)
Scope of incompatibility (same assertion, same endpoint, same programme)
Declaring authority and effective period

questions.text: Which governance acts require two distinct natural persons, and how is distinctness determined?
answer_data: Act codes requiring a two-person condition
Distinctness test (distinct agent identifier, distinct legal person, distinct reporting line)
Minimum number of concurring agents
Handling of software-agent participants

questions.text: When a duty conflict is observed on an existing assignment, what is recorded and who must act on it?
answer_data: Conflict observation record with detected archetype set
Observation timestamp and observing agent or tool
Accountable remediation agent
Referral note stating that blocking or revoking access is executed by the referenced access model
Link to any compensating exception grant

questions.text: How is cumulative privilege across delegated bindings assessed so that separation is not defeated by aggregation over time?
answer_data: Aggregation window definition
Set of bindings considered (direct and delegated)
History-based separation rule reference
Assessment outcome and assessing agent

data_elements.name: Incompatible duty set
data_elements.description: A named set of archetype codes declared not simultaneously holdable by one agent within a stated scope.

data_elements.name: Separation mode
data_elements.description: Whether the separation is static, dynamic at access time, or history-based over a defined window.

data_elements.name: Two-person condition
data_elements.description: Requirement that a named governance act be performed by two distinct persons, with the distinctness test applied.

data_elements.name: Duty conflict observation
data_elements.description: Recorded observation that a binding set violates a declared incompatible duty set, with observation time and observer.

artifacts.name: Incompatible-duty matrix
artifacts.description: The declarative matrix of archetype combinations, separation modes, two-person conditions and scopes, published as governed constraint data that an external policy decision point can consume as attributes. It states rules and does not evaluate them.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the adopting Dimension's master-system identifier for the governance ruleset, plus a monotonically increasing ruleset version; individual rows are identified by the ordered archetype-code tuple and scope code.

layers.name: Role Binding, Delegation and Mandatory Qualifiers
layers.description: How an abstract archetype becomes a concrete, time-bounded accountability of a named agent, including delegation chains and acting-on-behalf-of relationships, and the purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers that every governance act must carry so that the record is interpretable outside its originating context.

findings.name: Role binding, term and delegation chain
findings.description: The qualified attribution that binds one archetype to one agent for a stated scope of dependency or impact assertions over a stated validity period, together with the delegation chain when an agent acts on behalf of another and the succession rule when a binding lapses. Modelled on the PROV-O qualified-attribution pattern and the validFrom/validUntil plus status pattern of verifiable credentials.

questions.text: How is a single role binding identified and distinguished from every other binding of the same agent and archetype?
answer_data: Binding identifier resolved by the identity priority rule
Bound agent reference
Archetype code
Scope expression (assertion set, endpoint set or domain)
Binding version or sequence number

questions.text: What states may a role binding occupy between proposal and termination, and what triggers each transition?
answer_data: State code (proposed, active, suspended, lapsed, revoked, superseded)
Transition trigger and triggering agent
Successor binding reference
Reason code for suspension or revocation

questions.text: When an agent acts on behalf of another for a governance act, how is the delegation chain recorded and bounded?
answer_data: Delegating agent reference
Delegate agent reference
Delegation depth and maximum permitted depth
Acts included in and excluded from the delegation
Delegation validity period

questions.text: Over which validity period is the binding effective, and how are effective time and record time distinguished?
answer_data: Valid-from timestamp
Valid-until timestamp or open-ended marker
Record creation timestamp
Observation or ingestion timestamp where it differs from the effective time
Time zone offset carried explicitly

data_elements.name: Role binding identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a single archetype-to-agent binding within a stated scope.

data_elements.name: Binding scope expression
data_elements.description: The set of dependency or impact assertions, endpoints or domains over which the binding is effective.

data_elements.name: Binding validity period
data_elements.description: Valid-from and optional valid-until instants for the binding, with explicit offsets.

data_elements.name: Binding state
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the binding with reason code and transition provenance.

data_elements.name: Delegation chain
data_elements.description: Ordered acted-on-behalf-of links from the performing agent to the ultimately accountable agent, with depth bound.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A role binding is a qualified attribution: a structured inline statement that links an already-identified agent, an archetype code from the register, a scope expression and a validity period to a dependency or impact assertion. Its authoritative constituents live elsewhere - agents in the party/agent identity model, archetype codes in the archetype register artifact, scope in the core assertion structure - so a standalone binding artifact would be a derived join with no independent authority and a high risk of drifting from its sources. Representing it inline keeps exactly one authoritative copy and makes the binding travel with the assertion it qualifies.

findings.name: Purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers on governance acts
findings.description: Every governance act recorded by this model must declare the purpose for which it was performed and the jurisdiction or territorial scope under which it is claimed to be valid. Both are carried as references into externally governed code lists - a purpose vocabulary and a jurisdiction registry - so that the model can require the qualifier without asserting any doctrine about what a jurisdiction is or which law prevails.

questions.text: For what declared purpose was this governance act performed, and from which governed vocabulary is that purpose drawn?
answer_data: Purpose code and source vocabulary identifier
Free-text purpose narrative where the code list is insufficient
Purpose declared at act time rather than inferred later
Reference to the compatibility assessment held in the referenced privacy model where the act touches personal data

questions.text: Which jurisdiction or territorial scope is claimed for this act, and how are multiple or conflicting claims represented?
answer_data: Jurisdiction code and registry reference
Territorial scope type (entity seat, data location, endpoint location, contractual forum)
Ordered list where several jurisdictions are claimed
Conflict marker with no local resolution rule

questions.text: Does the governance record contain personal data about the bound agent, and what minimisation applies?
answer_data: Personal-data present flag
Categories of personal data carried (identifier, role, contact reference)
Minimisation decision and its rationale
Reference to the controller determination held in the referenced privacy model

questions.text: How do purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers reach the systems that decide who may read the governance record?
answer_data: Qualifier attributes exposed for external decision points
Attribute naming and namespace
Statement that this model supplies attributes and renders no decision
Reference to the access and policy model that consumes them

data_elements.name: Governance purpose code
data_elements.description: Reference into an external purpose vocabulary stating why a governance act was performed.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction qualifier reference
data_elements.description: Reference into an external jurisdiction registry describing the territorial scope claimed for the act.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction conflict marker
data_elements.description: Marker that two or more claimed jurisdictions conflict, with no local resolution asserted.

data_elements.name: Personal-data presence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the governance record carries personal data, with the categories present.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Purpose and jurisdiction are mandatory qualifiers attached to each governance act, not documents in their own right. The vocabularies they point at are owned by external registries - a purpose code list and a jurisdiction registry - and reproducing either locally would create an unauthoritative copy and would drag polity doctrine into a model that must stay neutral. The model therefore carries only the coded reference, the scope type and a conflict marker as inline reference data on the act it qualifies.

bundles.name: Assurance, Exception and Record Governance
bundles.description: The governance acts that change the standing of a dependency or impact assertion after it has been issued: review and approval decisions, handling of contested or unresolvable assertions, time-bounded exception grants by a named authority, and the declarative record-governance markers that route the resulting records to the correct retention, hold and access regimes owned elsewhere.
bundles.rationale: Registration governance in RFC 8126 shows that an assertion's standing depends on a reviewer decision, a change controller's authority and an appeals path for contested cases; NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2 shows that an approval is an explicit acceptance of residual risk by a named authorizing official, tracked with a plan of action and milestones; SPDX distinguishes an assertion of no relationship from an absence of assertion, giving contested and unknown states first-class treatment; and NARA guidance plus GDPR storage limitation show that retention and legal-hold execution belong to a records authority rather than the originating system. This bundle records outcomes and referrals, never enforcement.

layers.name: Review, Approval and Contested Assertions
layers.description: The decision records that move a dependency or impact assertion from issued to reviewed to approved or rejected, and the parallel track for assertions whose truth or scope is disputed by a steward, an analyst or a counterparty.

findings.name: Review and approval decision record
findings.description: A separately attributed decision record stating that a named reviewer examined a dependency or impact assertion and that a named approver accepted or rejected it, with the decision outcome, its stated basis, the effective time of the decision and the conditions attached. Reviewer and approver are distinct archetypes: review establishes technical adequacy, approval constitutes acceptance of the residual consequence.

questions.text: What sequence of review and approval steps is required before a dependency or impact assertion is treated as governed, and what is the timeliness expectation for each?
answer_data: Ordered step list with the archetype competent for each
Response-time expectation per step
Conditions under which a step may be skipped
Recusal rule where the reviewer has a declared conflict of interest

questions.text: What governance standing does an assertion hold at any moment, and how is that standing represented when review has expired or been withdrawn?
answer_data: Standing code (issued, in review, approved, rejected, withdrawn, lapsed, superseded)
Standing effective timestamp
Superseding decision reference
Whether a lapsed approval reverts the assertion to in-review or to issued

questions.text: On what stated basis was the decision reached, and what supporting material is cited without being reproduced?
answer_data: Decision basis narrative
References to cited analyses, tests or attestations held elsewhere
Statement of what was not examined
Confidence or completeness qualifier attached to the reviewed assertion

questions.text: How is the adequacy of the review itself judged, and what makes a decision record defective?
answer_data: Minimum required fields for a valid decision record
Defect codes (missing basis, missing approver, expired binding, conflicted reviewer)
Re-review trigger conditions
Reviewer of the review where a second-line check applies

data_elements.name: Decision record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one review or approval decision on a dependency or impact assertion.

data_elements.name: Decision outcome
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of the governance act (approved, approved with conditions, rejected, returned for rework, withdrawn).

data_elements.name: Decision effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the decision takes effect, recorded separately from the instant the record was captured.

data_elements.name: Attached conditions
data_elements.description: Conditions the approver attached to an approval, each with an owner and a due date, tracked in the referenced risk or change model.

data_elements.name: Recusal or conflict note
data_elements.description: Record that a reviewer or approver recused themselves, with the declared conflict and the substitute agent.

artifacts.name: Dependency governance decision record
artifacts.description: An immutable, separately attributed record of one review or approval act on a named dependency or impact assertion, carrying outcome, basis, effective time, conditions, the acting agents and their bindings, and the purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers. Corrections are issued as superseding records rather than edits.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Primary identity is the adopting Dimension's master-system identifier from its governance or workflow system of record; where none exists, a governed IRI in the Dimension's decision namespace; failing both, a UUID or ULID minted at creation. Serial position is a monotonic sequence within the subject assertion, never derived from the decision date.

findings.name: Contested, unknown and no-assertion handling
findings.description: Treatment of dependency or impact assertions whose existence, direction, scope or severity is disputed. Distinguishes a positive assertion that no dependency exists from an absence of any assertion, records the contesting party and grounds, holds the assertion in a contested state without silently deleting it, and names the authority competent to resolve - including an escalation path when the contest crosses an organizational boundary.

questions.text: What event opened the contest, who raised it, and against which specific element of the assertion?
answer_data: Contest opening timestamp and raising agent
Contested element (existence, direction, endpoint, type, scope, severity, timing)
Contest ground narrative
Counter-assertion reference where one is offered

questions.text: How is a positive statement that no dependency exists distinguished from the absence of any statement, and from an unresolved contest?
answer_data: Assertion stance code (asserted, asserted-none, no-assertion, contested)
Stance provenance and asserting agent
Reason the stance could not be strengthened
Downstream handling rule for each stance

questions.text: Which authority is competent to resolve this contest, and what is the escalation path when the parties sit under different owners?
answer_data: Competent resolving authority reference
Escalation tier and next tier
Cross-boundary escalation route (contract governance, joint forum, external adjudicator)
Statement that unresolved cross-boundary contests remain open rather than defaulting to either party

questions.text: How long may a contest remain open, and what is recorded when it exceeds that period?
answer_data: Contest opened and target-resolution timestamps
Age threshold and breach marker
Interim treatment of the assertion while contested
Resolution or lapse timestamp and resolving agent

data_elements.name: Contest record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one open or closed contest against a dependency or impact assertion.

data_elements.name: Assertion stance code
data_elements.description: Coded stance distinguishing asserted, asserted-none, no-assertion and contested, following the SPDX distinction between a none element and a no-assertion element.

data_elements.name: Contested element
data_elements.description: The specific aspect of the assertion under dispute.

data_elements.name: Competent resolving authority
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent or forum competent to close the contest, with escalation tier.

data_elements.name: Interim treatment code
data_elements.description: How the assertion is to be treated by consumers while the contest is open.

artifacts.name: Contested assertion record
artifacts.description: A record of one contest: what is disputed, by whom, on what ground, any counter-assertion, the competent resolving authority, the interim treatment and the eventual resolution. Retained after closure so that the history of disputed dependency claims is reconstructable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Primary identity is the master-system identifier from the adopting Dimension's case or issue system of record; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension's contest namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID. Serial position is a monotonic sequence within the contested assertion and carries no date component.

layers.name: Exception Authority and Time-Bounded Waivers
layers.description: The narrow, explicitly bounded power to accept a documented deviation from the governance rules of this model - for example proceeding on an unacknowledged external dependency, or approving despite an observed duty conflict - vested in a named authority for a bounded period under stated conditions.

findings.name: Exception grant and accountable exception authority
findings.description: A record that a named exception authority, acting within a declared scope of competence, granted a time-bounded waiver of a specific governance requirement for a specific dependency or impact assertion, with the compensating conditions, the expiry and the named agent accountable for the residual consequence. Modelled on the authorization decision as an explicit, time-bounded acceptance of residual risk rather than a silent rule suppression.

questions.text: Which authority is competent to grant this exception, and what is the ceiling on that competence?
answer_data: Exception authority agent reference and binding
Competence ceiling expressed as requirement classes, impact severity or endpoint criticality
Requirements that may never be excepted
Escalation target where the request exceeds the ceiling

questions.text: Precisely which governance requirement is waived, for which assertions, and what remains in force?
answer_data: Waived requirement identifier
Assertion or endpoint scope of the waiver
Requirements explicitly not waived
Compensating conditions with owners

questions.text: When does the exception expire, and what is the recorded consequence of expiry without renewal?
answer_data: Granted-from and expires-at timestamps with explicit offsets
Maximum permitted duration by exception class
Renewal decision reference
Post-expiry standing of the affected assertion

questions.text: What constraints prevent an exception from becoming a permanent substitute for compliance?
answer_data: Maximum consecutive renewal count
Prohibition on self-granted exceptions
Requirement for a remediation reference in the referenced risk or change model
Periodic review obligation and its owner

data_elements.name: Exception grant identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one exception or waiver grant.

data_elements.name: Waived requirement reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the specific governance requirement of this model that is waived.

data_elements.name: Exception validity window
data_elements.description: Granted-from and expires-at instants bounding the waiver, with explicit offsets.

data_elements.name: Compensating condition
data_elements.description: A condition imposed as the price of the exception, with an accountable owner and a due date tracked externally.

data_elements.name: Residual accountable agent
data_elements.description: The agent accepting accountability for the consequence of the waived requirement.

artifacts.name: Exception grant record
artifacts.description: The signed, time-bounded record of a waiver: waived requirement, scope, compensating conditions, validity window, granting authority with its binding, residual accountable agent, and the purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers. Renewals are new records referencing the prior grant, never edits to it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Primary identity is the master-system identifier from the adopting Dimension's governance, risk and compliance system of record; otherwise a governed IRI in the Dimension's exception namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID. Serial position is a monotonic renewal sequence within the waived requirement and scope, with no date-derived component.

layers.name: Record-Governance Referral Markers
layers.description: The declarative markers this model places on its own governance records - sensitivity and access classification, retention-class reference and legal-hold marker - that let the owning access, privacy and records models apply the correct regime without this model deciding, enforcing or executing anything.

findings.name: Sensitivity, access, retention and legal-hold referral markers
findings.description: Governance records about dependencies are frequently sensitive: they name accountable individuals, expose organizational weak points and identify unacknowledged external reliance. This finding declares the markers carried on each governance record - a sensitivity and access classification supplied as attributes to the external decision point, a retention-class reference into the records model, and a legal-hold marker with its provenance - together with the explicit statement that classification is not authorization, that this model is not an audit store, and that suspension of disposition is executed and adjudicated elsewhere.

questions.text: How sensitive is this governance record, and on what basis was that classification assigned?
answer_data: Sensitivity classification code and scheme reference
Basis for the classification (personal data present, commercial confidence, security exposure of an unacknowledged dependency)
Classifying agent and classification timestamp
Reclassification trigger and review date

questions.text: Which attributes does this model expose so that an external decision point can decide who may read the record, and what does it deliberately not decide?
answer_data: Exposed attribute set and namespace
Statement that no permit or deny decision is rendered locally
Reference to the access and policy model that owns decision and enforcement
Handling of obligations or advice returned by the external decision point, which are discharged by the enforcement point and not here

questions.text: Which retention class applies to this governance record, and who owns the disposition decision and its execution?
answer_data: Retention class reference into the records model
Retention trigger event (decision effective time, exception expiry, contest closure)
Statement that disposition approval and execution belong to the records authority
Reference to the adopting Dimension's records officer or equivalent

questions.text: Is this governance record under a legal or investigative hold, and what does the marker permit and forbid locally?
answer_data: Hold marker with hold identifier and issuing authority reference
Hold applied and released timestamps
Statement that the marker suspends local disposition proposals only
Statement that the legal determination and any unauthorized-disposition reporting are owned by the records and legal functions

questions.text: How is the boundary maintained between a governance record held here and the audit trail held in the referenced audit model?
answer_data: Correlation identifier shared with the audit model
List of events this model emits versus events it stores
Statement that log integrity, tamper-evidence and audit retention are external
Reconciliation procedure when the two diverge

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Coded sensitivity of the governance record with a reference to the classification scheme used.

data_elements.name: Exposed access attribute set
data_elements.description: The attributes published for consumption by an external policy decision point; contains no decision outcome.

data_elements.name: Retention class reference
data_elements.description: Reference into the records retention model naming the schedule that governs this record.

data_elements.name: Legal hold marker
data_elements.description: Flag with hold identifier, issuing authority reference and applied or released timestamps, suspending local disposition proposals.

data_elements.name: Audit correlation identifier
data_elements.description: Shared identifier allowing the referenced audit model to correlate its trail entries with this governance record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These markers are qualifiers on records that already exist as artifacts elsewhere in this model - decision records, contest records and exception grants - and their authoritative content is owned by other models: the classification scheme by the adopting Dimension's information-classification policy, the retention class by the records model, the hold by the legal function, and the audit trail by the audit model. Creating a separate marker artifact would either duplicate those authoritative registers or imply that this model holds a disposition or hold register of its own, which would breach the ownership boundary the model is built to respect. The markers are therefore purely inline reference data carried on the governed record.

functions.name: Bind role archetype to agent
functions.description: Create a qualified attribution binding one role archetype from the register to an identified agent for a stated scope, validity window, purpose and jurisdiction, optionally recording a delegation chain.
inputs: Agent reference resolved in the referenced party/agent identity model
Role archetype code from the archetype register
Scope expression over dependency or impact assertions
outputs: Role binding record in state proposed or active
Binding identifier
Rejection reason where inputs are incomplete
preconditions: The archetype code exists and is not deprecated in the register
The agent reference resolves in the referenced identity model
Purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers are present
Any declared delegation does not exceed the permitted depth
effects: A new binding exists with an explicit validity window and provenance
The binding becomes available as an attribute to external decision points
No access is granted and no privilege is provisioned by this function

functions.name: Screen proposed binding for duty conflict
functions.description: Compare a proposed or existing set of bindings against the incompatible-duty matrix and return an advisory conflict finding with the matched rule, separation mode and aggregation window. Advisory only: the function reports, it does not block, revoke or enforce.
inputs: Candidate binding set for one agent
outputs: Conflict finding with matched incompatible duty sets or an explicit no-conflict result
Separation mode that triggered the match
Referral pointer to the access and policy model that owns any resulting decision
preconditions: An effective incompatible-duty matrix version is available
All candidate bindings resolve to archetype codes in the register
effects: A duty conflict observation record is created with observation time and observing agent or tool
The finding is exposed as an attribute for external evaluation
No binding is suspended, revoked or blocked by this function

functions.name: Record review or approval decision
functions.description: Capture an immutable decision record stating the outcome, basis, effective time, conditions and acting agents for a review or approval act on a dependency or impact assertion.
inputs: Subject dependency or impact assertion reference
Acting agent reference and its active binding
Outcome code and decision basis narrative
Decision effective time and record capture time
outputs: Serial decision record
Updated governance standing of the subject assertion
Correlation identifier emitted to the referenced audit model
preconditions: The acting agent holds an active binding to a competent archetype
Any applicable two-person condition is satisfied by distinct agents
No unmitigated duty conflict is open without a covering exception grant
The reviewer has not recused for a declared conflict of interest
effects: The subject assertion's governance standing changes to the recorded value
The decision record is immutable; corrections require a superseding record
An event is emitted for external audit capture; no audit trail is stored locally

functions.name: Open contest against an assertion
functions.description: Register a dispute over the existence, direction, scope, type, severity or timing of a dependency or impact assertion, set the assertion stance and interim treatment, and name the competent resolving authority.
inputs: Contested element codes and ground narrative
Proposed resolving authority and escalation tier
outputs: Serial contest record in open state
Updated assertion stance and interim treatment code
Escalation route where the contest crosses an organizational boundary
preconditions: The subject assertion exists and is not already tombstoned
The contesting agent is identified, whether or not it holds a binding
effects: The subject assertion is marked contested without being deleted or overwritten
Consumers are directed to the recorded interim treatment
A target resolution time is set and its breach becomes reportable

functions.name: Resolve or lapse a contest
functions.description: Close an open contest with a recorded resolution by the competent authority, or mark it lapsed when the resolution window expires without a decision, in both cases preserving the full contest history.
outputs: Closed or lapsed contest record
Resulting assertion stance
Referral to a higher escalation tier where resolution was not competent
preconditions: The contest is open
The resolving agent is the competent authority for the recorded escalation tier, or the lapse condition is met
effects: The contest record is closed with an immutable outcome
The assertion stance is updated, which may leave it asserted-none or no-assertion
Cross-boundary contests that no single party may close remain open rather than defaulting

functions.name: Grant or renew a time-bounded exception
functions.description: Record that a competent exception authority waived a specific governance requirement for a bounded scope and period under stated compensating conditions, naming the agent accountable for the residual consequence.
inputs: Scope of assertions or endpoints affected
Prior grant reference where this is a renewal
outputs: Serial exception grant record
Effective waiver window applied to the named scope
Renewal counter
preconditions: The requested waiver falls within the authority's declared competence ceiling
The requirement is not on the never-exceptable list
The exception authority is not the agent that requested it
Maximum consecutive renewal count is not exceeded
effects: The named requirement is recorded as waived for the stated scope and window only
A remediation reference in the referenced risk or change model becomes mandatory
On expiry without renewal the affected assertions revert to their pre-exception standing

functions.name: Set record-governance referral markers
functions.description: Assign or update the sensitivity classification, retention-class reference, legal-hold marker and audit correlation identifier on a governance record so that owning models can apply the correct regime.
inputs: Retention class reference and retention trigger event
Optional hold identifier, issuing authority and applied timestamp
outputs: Updated marker set on the governance record
Attribute payload published for external decision points
Reclassification review date
preconditions: The classification scheme and retention schedule references resolve in the owning models
A hold marker is accompanied by an issuing authority reference
effects: Markers become available to the access, privacy, records and audit models
Local disposition proposals for the record are suspended while a hold marker is set
No access decision is rendered and no record is destroyed by this function

functions.name: Resolve accountable parties for an assertion
functions.description: Given a dependency or impact assertion, a governance act, a purpose and a jurisdiction, return the currently bound agents competent for that act, their delegation chains and any unresolved accountability gaps. This is a lookup over declared bindings, not an authorization check.
outputs: Ordered list of competent bound agents with binding identifiers
Delegation chain for each
Gap report where no competent binding exists or all bindings have lapsed
preconditions: Bindings exist and their validity windows are expressed with explicit offsets
The archetype register version in force at the evaluation instant is resolvable
effects: A point-in-time accountability view is produced and can be cited by other models
Gaps are surfaced as unstewarded or unbound conditions requiring escalation
No permission is granted and no obligation is discharged by this function

composition.target: WM-XCT-037 core dependency and impact assertion structure (typed edges, traversal, impact propagation)
composition.purpose: Attach governance-role semantics to each dependency or impact assertion without owning edge typing, graph construction, transitive closure or blast-radius computation, which remain in the host structure and follow patterns such as the SPDX Relationship from/to/relationshipType/completeness shape and CycloneDX dependency graphs.

composition.target: Party, organization and agent identity model
composition.purpose: Resolve the agent identifiers that role bindings, decisions, contests and exception grants point at. This model carries only the reference and the role qualification; minting, merging and retiring agent identities stay in the identity model.

composition.target: Access-control and authorization policy model (policy administration, decision, enforcement and information points)
composition.purpose: Publish role bindings, incompatible-duty declarations, sensitivity classifications and purpose or jurisdiction qualifiers as attributes for external policy evaluation. Rendering permit or deny decisions, enforcing them and discharging obligations or advice are owned entirely by that model; nothing here grants or denies access.

composition.target: Audit trail and evidence record model
composition.purpose: Emit correlation identifiers and governance events for capture in the audit trail. Log integrity, tamper-evidence, non-repudiation, audit retention and audit reporting are owned by that model; this model stores governance outcomes, not audit records.

composition.target: Records retention, disposition and legal-hold model
composition.purpose: Carry a retention-class reference and a legal-hold marker on this model's governance records. Schedule approval, disposition execution, retention extension for litigation, hold release and unauthorized-disposition reporting are owned by that model and the adopting Dimension's records authority.

Refer purpose-limitation compatibility assessment, lawful-basis determination, controller and processor allocation, and records of processing activities outward, while requiring a purpose qualifier and a personal-data presence flag on every governance act recorded here.

Supply the coded jurisdiction values used as mandatory qualifiers, so that the model can require a jurisdiction without defining jurisdictions, asserting precedence between them or embedding polity doctrine.

composition.target: Risk management, change and release management models
composition.purpose: Hold the remediation plans, conditions with due dates and risk-treatment decisions that exception grants and conditional approvals point at. This model records the governance outcome and its accountable authority, not the treatment methodology or its tracking.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O qualified attribution and delegation pattern
composition.purpose: Align role binding on the qualified-attribution pattern (agent, role, influence) and delegation on acted-on-behalf-of, so governance provenance is exchangeable. Alignment only: no conformance to PROV-O is claimed without a published mapping and validation evidence.

composition.target: SPDX 3.0.1 Core model (Element, CreationInfo, Annotation, Relationship stance semantics)
composition.purpose: Align issuer attribution on CreationInfo, independently attributed review commentary on Annotation, and the asserted-none versus no-assertion distinction on the SPDX none and no-assertion element semantics. Alignment only; no SPDX conformance is claimed.

composition.target: W3C ODRL Vocabulary and Expression 2.2 party functions and constraint operands
composition.purpose: Align observer and informed-party archetypes on ODRL party functions and align purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers on the purpose and spatial constraint left operands, for exchange with policy expression tooling. Alignment only; this model expresses no permissions, prohibitions or duties.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension governance role archetype extension package
composition.purpose: Allow a Dimension to specialise the seven generic archetypes with local roles under a declared parent archetype and its own registration policy, without duplicating the generic identity, delegation, contest or exception machinery defined here.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single accountable owner for the governance-role overlay and for the archetype register, distinct from the owner of the dependency-graph core it mixes into.
The Dimension must publish the mapping from the seven generic archetypes to its own organizational roles, committees and delegated bodies, and keep that mapping versioned.

The Dimension must nominate the referenced models that own access decisions, audit storage, party identity, retention and disposition, privacy, jurisdiction codes and risk or change tracking before any governance record is created, and must record a gap where a referenced model does not yet exist.
The Dimension must declare its purpose vocabulary, jurisdiction registry and sensitivity classification scheme, or explicitly adopt an external one.
The Dimension must set the competence ceilings, never-exceptable requirement list and maximum renewal counts for exception authorities before the exception function is enabled.
dimension.namespace_guidance: All identifiers minted by this overlay live in a Dimension-scoped namespace segregated by concern: archetype codes, binding identifiers, decision records, contest records and exception grants each occupy a distinct sub-namespace so that a local extension never collides with a generic archetype code. Generic archetype codes are reserved and may not be redefined locally; a Dimension-local archetype must be minted in the extension sub-namespace and declare its parent. Namespaces are format-neutral: the same identifier resolves identically whether projected to a document store, a graph, a Git tree or an interface response.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 under nav path NAV.XCT.DEP, domain tag XCT.DEP, entry kind mixin
Governed archetype register published as a versioned controlled vocabulary with reserved and deprecated statuses following registration-policy practice in RFC 8126
Referenced external registries: purpose vocabulary, jurisdiction registry, sensitivity classification scheme and party/agent identity register, each cited by identifier and version

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the semantic record, not a serialisation: archetype code, agent reference, scope expression, validity window, purpose, jurisdiction, outcome and provenance. Any JSON, YAML, Markdown, graph or database projection must round-trip these without loss.

Agent, jurisdiction, purpose, retention-class and classification values are canonicalised as references to their owning registry plus the registry version in force at the act's effective time; resolved labels are cache, never canon.

Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 date-time with two-digit seconds and an explicit offset or Z; the originating offset is preserved rather than normalised to UTC, because the offset is governance-relevant evidence of where an act occurred.
Ordering of collections that carry no declared semantics (for example excluded acts) is normalised by code before comparison, so that reordering is not treated as a change.
Free text carries an explicit language tag; absence of a tag is a validation defect, not a default to English.
patch_rules: Decision records, contest records and exception grants are immutable once created. A correction is a new superseding record that cites the record it supersedes; the superseded record is retained with a superseded marker.
Role bindings are versioned rather than edited: a change of scope, archetype or validity produces a successor binding and closes the predecessor with a reason code and a transition timestamp.
Archetype register entries are never deleted. Withdrawal is expressed as a deprecated or obsolete status with a successor reference, following registration-registry practice.

A patch that would change the accountable agent, the outcome of a decision, the waived requirement of an exception or a legal-hold marker requires the same competence as the original act and is recorded as a distinct governance act.
Patches must state the effective time of the change separately from the time the patch was recorded.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new archetype, outcome code, contest element or separation mode is a minor change; consumers must tolerate unknown codes by treating the record as ungoverned-unknown rather than discarding it.

Removing or narrowing the meaning of an existing archetype code, or making a previously optional qualifier mandatory, is a breaking change requiring a major version and a stated migration for existing bindings.
Alignments to PROV-O, SPDX and ODRL are advisory mappings; a change in an aligned external vocabulary does not by itself break this model, but the mapping version must be restated and re-validated.
A projection that cannot carry an explicit time offset, a superseding reference or a language tag is non-conformant and must not be used as the system of record.
Consumers must not infer authorization from any field in this model; a projection that presents classification or binding data as an access grant is a breaking misuse.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the subject - the adopting Dimension's identity, human-resources, governance-risk-and-compliance, case or workflow master record key for the agent, binding, decision, contest or exception concerned.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the Dimension's published governance namespace where no master-system identifier exists, resolvable and stable across projections.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as a last resort, recorded together with the reason no higher-priority identifier was available.
A date, timestamp, sequence position, agent name, job title or role label is never an identifier; serial position and effective date are attributes of an already-identified record.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time with two-digit seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; a bare local time or an omitted offset is a validation defect, and -00:00 is used only where the local offset is genuinely unknown. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they differ: a decision carries its effective time (when the approval, rejection, contest opening, resolution or waiver takes effect) distinctly from its record capture time (when the governance system received it), and a binding carries valid-from and valid-until distinctly from the instant the binding record was created. Where a governance act is reported by a third party, the reporting time is recorded as a third instant alongside the asserted event time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - decision records, contest records and exception grants - are numbered by a monotonically increasing integer sequence scoped to their subject (the dependency or impact assertion for decisions and contests; the waived requirement plus scope for exception renewals). The sequence never encodes a date, a year, an agent identifier or an outcome, and gaps are permitted and must not be back-filled. The serial is a qualifier of an identified record, never its identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each artifact records its creating agent, creating tool where applicable, creation instant and the register or ruleset version in force, following the requirement that every assertion element carry creation attribution. Immutable artifacts should carry a content digest or detached signature so that later reproduction is verifiable; where a digest is absent, the artifact is marked unverifiable rather than presumed intact. Verification of a signature establishes authorship only; whether the record is fit to be relied on for a given purpose is a separate validation performed by the consumer, and neither verification nor validation is performed by this model.

policies: Declarative, non-enforcing: this model records role archetypes, bindings, duty constraints, decisions, contests, exceptions and referral markers. It renders no authorization decision, enforces no policy, provisions no privilege and stores no audit trail; those belong to the referenced access, policy and audit models.

Mandatory qualification: no governance act may be recorded without an identified acting agent, an active binding to a competent archetype, a purpose code and a jurisdiction reference, each drawn from a governed external vocabulary.

No silent deletion of contested or superseded governance content: contests, superseded decisions and expired exceptions are retained with status markers so that the governance history of a dependency claim remains reconstructable.

Self-review and self-approval are prohibited by default; an exception to a segregation rule must itself be an explicit, time-bounded, separately authorised exception grant and can never be granted by the requesting agent.

Referral honesty: where a concept is owned by another model, this model stores only the reference and the qualifier, and records a gap rather than fabricating a local substitute when the owning model is absent.
Neutrality: archetypes, purposes and jurisdictions are carried as codes from external registries; the model asserts no precedence between jurisdictions, no organizational form and no legal doctrine.

read: Read of an archetype register entry or the incompatible-duty matrix is open to any agent with a legitimate governance purpose, since these are rule declarations rather than case data.

Read of bindings, decisions, contests, exception grants and their markers is mediated by the referenced access model using the attributes this model publishes; this model returns records only after that external decision permits it.
Point-in-time reads must resolve the register and ruleset version in force at the requested instant, not the current version.
Reads that would expose personal data in a binding must honour the minimisation decision recorded on that binding.
create: Creation of a role binding requires a resolvable agent reference, a non-deprecated archetype code, a scope expression, a validity window with explicit offsets, and purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers.

Creation of a decision, contest or exception record requires an acting agent holding an active binding to a competent archetype and, where applicable, satisfaction of the two-person condition by distinct persons.
Creation is refused where a required referenced model is unavailable to resolve an obligatory reference; the attempt is recorded as a gap rather than completed with a placeholder.
Every created record captures its creating agent, creating tool, creation instant and the register or ruleset version in force.
update: Immutable records (decisions, contests once closed, exception grants) are never updated in place; a superseding record is created that cites its predecessor.
Role bindings are updated only by versioned succession: the predecessor is closed with a reason code and transition timestamp and a successor is created.
Archetype register entries change status (active, deprecated, obsolete) with a successor reference; definitions are not silently rewritten.

Marker updates (classification, retention class, hold) record the changing agent, the change instant and the prior value, and a hold marker may be released only on the authority of the referenced records or legal function.
delete: This model does not destroy governance records on its own authority. Removal is expressed as a tombstone: the record identifier, its record type, its supersession or closure status, the disposition authority reference and the disposition instant are retained after content is redacted or removed, so that references from other models do not dangle.

Every governance record carries a retention-class reference and a retention trigger event (decision effective time, contest closure, exception expiry, binding termination); the applicable schedule and the approval of disposition are owned by the referenced records retention and disposition model, and execution is performed by the adopting Dimension's records authority, not by this model.

While a legal-hold marker is set, this model must not propose or permit disposition of the marked record; the legal determination that a hold applies, its scope, its release and any extension of retention for litigation are owned by the referenced records model and the Dimension's legal function.

Where a governance record contains personal data, erasure or restriction requests are routed to the referenced privacy model, which determines the outcome; this model applies the resulting instruction as a redaction plus tombstone and records the instruction's source.

Unauthorized, accidental or premature removal is reported to the Dimension's records authority under its own reporting obligations; this model records that a report was made and its reference, and does not adjudicate the incident.

roles.name: Model owner (adopting Dimension)
responsibilities: Own the governance-role overlay, its archetype register and its incompatible-duty matrix, and approve versioned changes to them.
Name the referenced models for access, audit, identity, retention, privacy, jurisdiction and risk, and record gaps where they are absent.
Set competence ceilings, never-exceptable requirements and maximum renewal counts for exception authorities.

roles.name: Register steward
responsibilities: Maintain archetype codes, definitions, competent and excluded acts, parent links and external mappings.
Apply deprecation and obsolescence statuses with successor references rather than deleting entries.
Review and admit Dimension-local archetype extensions against the declared registration policy.

roles.name: Governance reviewer
responsibilities: Examine dependency and impact assertions for technical adequacy and record a decision basis, including what was not examined.
Respond within the declared timeliness expectation and recuse on any declared conflict of interest.
Raise a contest where an assertion appears wrong rather than silently amending it.

roles.name: Approving authority
responsibilities: Accept or reject a reviewed assertion and thereby accept the residual consequence, attaching conditions with named owners and due dates tracked externally.
Refuse approval where a two-person condition, an active binding or a duty-conflict resolution is missing.
Ensure approval decisions carry effective time, purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers.

roles.name: Exception authority
responsibilities: Grant, refuse or renew time-bounded waivers strictly within a declared competence ceiling and never on their own request.
Record compensating conditions, the residual accountable agent and a mandatory remediation reference in the referenced risk or change model.
Escalate any request that exceeds the ceiling or touches a never-exceptable requirement.

roles.name: Endpoint steward
responsibilities: Accept or dispute stewardship of a named end of a dependency, and record the control-boundary classification.
Acknowledge or contest assertions naming their endpoint, and flag unstewarded endpoints for escalation.
Maintain the contract or agreement reference where the endpoint sits outside the adopting Dimension.

roles.name: Record-governance liaison
responsibilities: Assign sensitivity classifications, retention-class references and audit correlation identifiers to governance records.
Apply and release legal-hold markers only on instruction from the referenced records or legal function.
Route erasure, restriction and disposition requests to the owning models and record the instruction source and outcome.

roles.name: Observer / informed party
responsibilities: Receive notification of governance acts affecting an endpoint or impact path of declared interest, with read-only standing.
Hold no competence to review, approve, except or resolve, and no accountability for the assertion's correctness.
Raise a contest as any identified agent may, without that raising conferring resolving authority.

access.default_rule: Deny by default at the referenced access model, which is the sole decision point. This model publishes attributes - archetype bindings, delegation chains, incompatible-duty findings, sensitivity classification, purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers, hold and retention markers - and returns a record only after that external decision permits. Holding a governance archetype confers competence to be recorded as the actor of a governance act; it confers no read or write privilege on any system, including this one.
exceptions: Archetype register entries and the incompatible-duty matrix are readable without case-level authorization because they are published rule declarations containing no case data or personal data.

An endpoint steward named on an assertion may read the governance standing and open decisions for that assertion even where broader case access is denied, so that accountability is not asserted against an agent kept unaware of it.
A contesting agent may read the contest record it raised and its resolution, including where the underlying assertion is otherwise restricted, limited to the contested elements.

Records under a legal-hold marker may be subject to a preservation-driven access exception granted by the referenced records or legal function; this model records that the exception exists and its authority, and does not evaluate it.

Break-glass access asserted during an incident is recorded here only as a marker with its asserting authority and instant; its authorisation and review belong to the referenced access and audit models.
