audit_requirements: Every governance act emits an event carrying the acting agent, binding identifier, act code, effective time, record time, purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers, and an audit correlation identifier, for capture by the referenced audit model.

This model retains no audit trail: log integrity, tamper-evidence, non-repudiation, audit retention and audit reporting are owned externally, and divergence between the two is reconciled by the documented reconciliation procedure.
Read events on restricted governance records are logged by the enforcing access model, not by this model; this model records only the correlation identifier it published.

Duty-conflict observations, recusals, hold applications and releases, tombstone creations and superseding records must each emit a distinct event so the governance history is externally reconstructable.
Absence of an expected correlation identifier in the audit model is a reportable integrity gap for the model owner, not something this model may repair by writing its own audit entry.

required_fields: Registers in force (archetype register and incompatible-duty matrix versions)
Non-ownership statement (grants no access, enforces no policy, computes no impact propagation, stores no audit trail)
read_order: AGENTS.md - establishes Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL, Processes URL, referenced models and the non-ownership statement
Model specification - scope, exclusions and boundary notes, read before any structural interpretation
Archetype register and incompatible-duty matrix at the version in force - required to interpret any binding or decision record
Referenced access and policy model - required before attempting any read of case-level governance data
Referenced retention, privacy and audit models - required before creating, marking or proposing disposition of any governance record
Host WM-XCT-037 core assertion structure - required to resolve the assertions that governance records qualify

coverage.claim: This is a bounded governance-role slice of WM-XCT-037, not the whole model. Within its assigned surface - role archetypes and accountability boundaries, binding and delegation, purpose and jurisdiction qualifiers, review and approval, contested assertions, exception authority, and record-governance referral markers - the structure is grounded in sixteen live primary sources from eight independent organizations (W3C, SPDX/Linux Foundation, IETF, OASIS, NIST, the European Union, NARA and Ecma International). Dependency-graph semantics, impact propagation, authorization decision-making, enforcement, audit storage, identity minting and disposition execution are deliberately excluded and routed to composition links. No conformance to any external standard is claimed; all external standards are recorded as alignments requiring separate mapping evidence.

checklist.notes: Identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI, then UUID/ULID with a recorded reason. Bindings, decisions, contests and exception grants each have an identifier element; serial position, dates, names and role labels are explicitly excluded as identifiers. Grounded in SRC-003 and SRC-005 for attribution and status, SRC-007 for registry entry identity.

Binding states (proposed, active, suspended, lapsed, revoked, superseded), assertion governance standing (issued, in review, approved, rejected, withdrawn, lapsed, superseded), contest open/closed/lapsed and exception granted/expired/renewed are all modelled with triggers and successors. The lifecycle of the dependency edge itself is not modelled here - it belongs to the host core.

Endpoint stewardship models both ends of an assertion with control-boundary classification and counterparty acknowledgement; delegation chains model agent-to-agent relationships; composition links declare eight outward REFERENCE relations, three ALIGN relations, one MIX-IN and one EXTEND. Edge typing between the dependency endpoints is out of scope.

RFC 3339 with two-digit seconds and explicit offset is mandated; effective time, record capture time, third-party reporting time, validity windows and exception expiry are separated. The originating offset is preserved rather than normalised because it is governance-relevant evidence. Grounded in SRC-008 and SRC-003.

Every governance act records acting agent, creating tool, creation instant, binding identifier and ruleset version in force, following the qualified-attribution and creation-attribution patterns in SRC-001 and SRC-003. Delegation is recorded as an acted-on-behalf-of chain with a depth bound.

Endpoint stewardship, residual accountable agent on exceptions, competent resolving authority on contests, and eight named service-layer roles with explicit responsibilities. Accountability boundaries are stated per archetype including excluded acts with a referral target. Grounded in SRC-011 and SRC-012.

Decision-record defect codes, two-person distinctness tests, duty-conflict screening, minimum required fields and function preconditions provide falsifiable validation. Note the deliberate separation, taken from SRC-005, between verification of authorship and validation of fitness for a consumer's purpose - the latter is not performed here.

Deny-by-default at the referenced external decision point; this model publishes attributes only and renders no decision, consistent with the PAP/PDP/PEP/PIP separation in SRC-009. Five named exceptions including endpoint-steward visibility of assertions naming them, and break-glass recorded as a marker only.

Every governance record carries a retention-class reference and a retention trigger event; deletion is tombstone-plus-redaction only. Schedule approval, disposition execution, retention extension for litigation, hold release and unauthorized-disposition adjudication are owned by the referenced records model and the Dimension's records authority, grounded in SRC-015 and SRC-014.

Alignments recorded to PROV-O, SPDX 3.0.1 Core and ODRL 2.2 with mapping strength and mismatch notes, plus explicit non-conformance claims. Compatibility rules require tolerance of unknown codes and forbid projections that cannot carry offsets, supersession references or language tags.

Static, dynamic and history-based separation modes, incompatible duty sets, two-person conditions and privilege-aggregation windows are declared as constraint data, following the NIST definition in SRC-013. Evaluation and blocking are explicitly external, consistent with SRC-009.

Time-bounded grants with competence ceilings, never-exceptable requirement lists, prohibition on self-granting, renewal counters, compensating conditions and mandatory external remediation references. Modelled on the authorization decision as explicit residual-risk acceptance in SRC-011.

Four-valued stance (asserted, asserted-none, no-assertion, contested) taken from the SPDX none-versus-no-assertion distinction in SRC-002, with competent resolving authority, cross-boundary escalation, interim treatment and an explicit rule that unresolved cross-boundary contests stay open rather than defaulting to either party. Appeals practice from SRC-007.

Mandatory purpose code and personal-data presence flag with a recorded minimisation decision; lawful basis, purpose-limitation compatibility, controller determination and data-subject rights are routed to the referenced privacy model per SRC-014, with purpose expressed via the ODRL purpose operand pattern in SRC-006.

The model mandates a jurisdiction reference and represents multi-claim and conflict cases, but deliberately asserts no precedence rule and depends on an external jurisdiction registry that is not yet nominated in the registry entry. Marked a gap rather than presented as canonical: without a named registry, jurisdiction codes are locally minted and non-interoperable.

Impact severity, criticality scoring and blast-radius quantification are measurement concerns owned by the host WM-XCT-037 core and the referenced risk model. This overlay records only that a severity claim was contested or approved, never the measurement itself.

known_omissions: Notification transport, subscription and delivery guarantees for the observer archetype are not modelled; only the standing and the fact of a notified-party relationship are captured.

No machine-readable expression syntax is specified for scope expressions or incompatible-duty rules; the model declares the semantics and leaves the expression language to the adopting Dimension, which limits immediate automation.
Cross-Dimension federation of role bindings - mutual recognition of another Dimension's archetypes and decisions - is not modelled; only the mapping-strength alignment mechanism exists.
The three ALIGN links to PROV-O, SPDX and ODRL are asserted from documented patterns but no published mapping file or validation report exists yet, so conformance is not claimed.

Bulk or programmatic governance acts by software agents at scale (for example automated re-approval on rebuild) are permitted by the Agent typing in SRC-003 but their competence limits are not bounded here.
Cost, effort and timeliness metrics for the governance process are omitted as operational management concerns.
The interaction between an exception grant and an active legal hold is not resolved: whether an expiry may lapse a record that must be preserved is left to the referenced records model.
conflicts: RFC 8126 vests approval of future modification in a single Change Controller, while NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2 separates the system owner from the authorizing official who accepts risk. This model does not merge them: it keeps endpoint steward and approving authority distinct and lets the adopting Dimension collapse them only by an explicit, recorded mapping.

SPDX CreationInfo treats created as the time of last modification of the described thing (supporting reproducible builds), whereas governance practice needs the time the governance act took effect. The model resolves this by recording effective time, record time and reporting time separately rather than reusing a single created field.

ODRL models parties inside enforceable rules with permissions, prohibitions and duties; this model borrows only the party-function and constraint-operand vocabulary and expresses no rule, because expressing a permission here would breach the non-enforcement boundary.

GDPR storage limitation requires erasure once the purpose is exhausted, while records and litigation-hold regimes require preservation. This model carries both markers and refuses to arbitrate, routing the conflict to the referenced privacy and records models.

NIST separation-of-duty guidance anticipates enforcement at access time (dynamic separation), whereas this model can only declare the constraint. A Dimension that adopts this model without a functioning external decision point will have declared but unenforced separation - a real and reportable weakness, not a modelling artefact.

The registry entry lists factor_overlap at 0.06 and no aligned model identifiers, yet this slice necessarily depends on access, audit, identity, retention and privacy models. Either those siblings exist and the relation ledger is incomplete, or they do not and the required composition links are unsatisfiable gaps.
regional_assumptions: NARA guidance on unauthorized dispositions and the 44 U.S.C. 3106 reporting obligation is United States federal practice cited as an authoritative example of records-authority ownership; non-US Dimensions must substitute their own records regime and reporting obligation.

GDPR articles are cited as an authoritative example of purpose limitation, storage limitation, accountability and controller/processor allocation; Dimensions outside the EU/EEA must map to their equivalent instruments, and the model requires the qualifier without assuming GDPR applies.
NIST SP 800-53, 800-37 and 800-161 are US federal guidance used here for role archetypes and control-family separation; their control identifiers are not assumed to be binding on any Dimension.

The jurisdiction qualifier assumes a Dimension can name a single registry of territorial scopes. In federal, plurinational or extraterritorial settings multiple registries may apply and the conflict marker will be set frequently.

Two-person conditions assume a Dimension large enough to field two distinct competent persons; small Dimensions will rely disproportionately on the exception mechanism, which the renewal cap is intended to make visible.
adversarial_checks: Does any bundle, layer, finding or function grant, deny or evaluate access? Checked: the access-attribute finding, the duty-conflict screening function and the accountable-party resolution function were each written to publish attributes or return a lookup only, with explicit statements that no permission is granted and no obligation discharged. Obligations and advice are noted as discharged by the external enforcement point.

Does any element constitute an audit trail? Checked: decision, contest and exception records state outcomes and are immutable, but the model emits correlation identifiers and explicitly disclaims log integrity, tamper-evidence, audit retention and audit reporting; the access layer forbids this model from writing its own audit entry even to repair a gap.

Does the model duplicate the host WM-XCT-037 core? Checked: no edge typing, traversal, transitive closure, blast-radius or criticality computation appears in any finding or data element; measurement is marked not-applicable and routed to the core and risk models via boundary notes and composition links.

Could an attractive but unsupported structure have crept in? An 'impact severity governance' layer and a 'notification and escalation workflow' layer were considered and rejected: severity is a measurement owned by the core and risk models, and notification transport is operational messaging with no primary support for placing it in a governance-role overlay. Both are recorded as known omissions rather than modelled.

Is the exception mechanism a loophole that swallows the rules? Countered by competence ceilings, a never-exceptable requirement list, a prohibition on self-granting, mandatory expiry with explicit offsets, renewal counters and a mandatory external remediation reference - but a Dimension that leaves the ceiling undefined would have an unbounded waiver power, which is why defining it is a stated owner-package requirement.

Does any archetype embed organizational or polity doctrine? Checked: archetypes are abstract role concepts with a Dimension-owned mapping to local titles; purpose and jurisdiction are external code references with no precedence rule; the model asserts no committee structure, no reporting line and no legal hierarchy.

Can the deletion rule be used to erase inconvenient governance history? Countered by tombstone-plus-redaction retaining identifier, type, status, disposition authority and instant; by the prohibition on disposition while a hold marker is set; and by routing erasure instructions through the privacy model with the instruction source recorded. The residual risk is that this model cannot detect a records authority acting improperly, which is stated rather than papered over.

Are the composition targets real? Checked and flagged: the known-relation ledger for vr.wm-xct-037 is empty, so all twelve composition links are proposals rather than confirmed siblings. This is recorded as a conflict, and the owner-package requirements demand that missing referenced models be recorded as gaps rather than substituted locally.
